intended_object: The pullback (inverse image) functor f^* on sheaves of modules, for a morphism of ringed sites given by a continuous functor F and a ring map φ : S → F_* R. It is defined as the left adjoint of the pushforward f_*. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
In the literature, for a morphism of ringed sites/topoi the pullback f^* on modules is defined, up to unique isomorphism, as the left adjoint of the pushforward f_*. Classically it is built as f^{-1}M ⊗_{f^{-1}O} O, but this is characterised by the same adjunction.

The definition takes the left adjoint of `pushforward φ` under the hypothesis `IsRightAdjoint`, which is exactly that characterisation. The setting is general: any categories, any Grothendieck topologies, any continuous functor, and sheaves of rings. So the definition is not too narrow.

Assuming the left adjoint exists, instead of constructing it, is a reasonable design choice. It gives the right object whenever the pullback exists, and the existence of the left adjoint is a separate result. I found no other Mathlib declaration that defines this same object.
